subject: Urgent: ClearWave production 5xx surge post-quant roll (exec attention)
messages:
From: James Patel <j.patel@clearwave.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in 5xx/429 after your overnight config change

Markus / Marissa —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx (internal server) and 429 responses from Redwood's API starting ~02:30 UTC after the roll of the new quantization profile you shipped overnight. Impact: our production ML endpoint (prod-finbeat) has seen request success drop from 99.8% to ~86% and tail latency spiking to 3-6s. Customers are noticing timeouts in the UI.

Attached a small sample of error traces and a CSV of request ids where we see repeated retries. We pushed a temporary client-side retry backoff but end users still hit timeouts. This is affecting our week-one adoption for a major retail partner.

Can you confirm whether this rollout included a kernel change or a quant profile swap? We were not notified of a breaking rollout window. We need an estimate for mitigation time and whether you can revert to previous profile.

Thanks,
James Patel
Head of Platform
ClearWave Analytics

Attachments: error-sample-5xx.log, canary-requests.csv

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: James Patel <j.patel@clearwave.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 after your overnight config change

James — thanks for the prompt alert and the artifacts. We're on it. Quick update:

- I see the error pattern in our monitoring as well (alert fired at 02:40 UTC).
- We rolled a quantization profile v2.1.4 into the host pool at 02:20 UTC for the model variant you use (finbeat-v3-q4_0). No kernel-level changes were pushed this cycle.
- Initial hypothesis: the quant profile increased numerical instability for long-context requests and triggered elevated internal errors + downstream retry storms.

Action plan (immediate):
1) Marissa and Hannah will validate canary logs and confirm whether the canary cluster also shows the same 5xx/429 pattern.
2) If confirmed, we will execute a targeted rollback to v2.1.0 on the finbeat host pool and route traffic to the last-known-good variant.
3) Rishi will prepare a temporary routing rule to divert traffic to dedicated nodes and tweak rate-limiters / circuit breakers to prevent retry amplification.

I'll set up an exec slack bridge and loop in Sales leadership for customer comms. Expect a status update within 45 minutes.

— Markus Klein
Sr. Director, Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Cc: james.patel@clearwave.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 after your overnight config change

Markus / team — diagnostics from canary and prod partial roll: see attached metrics screenshot and request sample. Summary:

- Canary (10% of traffic) shows error ratio jump at the same time window; the failure mode is a mix of 5xx with \"tensor overflow\" traces and immediate 429s where the serving layer rejects requests due to queue backpressure.
- Error stack suggests quant rounding in attention kernels for long sequences; failures concentrate on requests with >1024 tokens.
- We observed increased retry rates from the ClearWave client (multiple identical request-ids in canary-requests.csv) leading to queue saturation.

Proposed steps (execute now):
A) Rollback quant profile to v2.1.0 for finbeat-v3-q4_0 hosts (targeted, not global). Estimated 7-10 min to propagate.
B) Flip routing: send ClearWave production traffic to dedicated fallback nodes (finbeat-legacy) while we validate.
C) Apply a temporary request deduplication + incremental backoff rule at the LB to protect the queue.

I'll start the rollback and report progress. If the rollback does not stabilize metrics within 15 minutes, we should escalate to full traffic shift and open an incident call.

Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: svc-metrics-20270315.png, canary-requests.csv

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 after your overnight config change

Marissa — saw the same traces. Additional notes from runtime:

- Kernel mismatch unlikely (no kernel deploy), but quant profile v2.1.4 enables an aggressive per-layer scale that appears to push fp16 quant pathways into an instability corner on long sequences.
- Canary nodes that use fallback_kernel_x show fewer tensor overflow traces — suggests behavior is sensitivity to kernel+quant interaction at certain sequence lengths.

Immediate mitigations I've applied (09:00 PST):
- Rolled a targeted rollback of finbeat-v3-q4_0 -> v2.1.0 on the host pool (rolling restart started).
- Added a temporary routing rule: route ClearWave traffic to finbeat-legacy nodes during the rollback window.
- Set LB policy: max concurrent per-client=6 and soft-429 backoff header instructing clients to back off exponentially.

Next: monitor 5xx/429 rate for 20m; if not improving, escalate to full variant revert and open exec incident bridge.

Commands run:
> redwood infra deploy --pool finbeat-hosts --model finbeat-v3-q4_0 --quant-profile v2.1.0 --targeted
> redwood route update --selector account=clearwave --destination finbeat-legacy

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

James / Olivia — follow-up after the rollback and today's actions:

What we did (summary):
- 09:03 PST (Mar 15): executed targeted rollback of quant profile to v2.1.0 on finbeat host pool for your account.
- 09:10 PST: traffic routed to finbeat-legacy nodes while we validated.
- 09:20 PST: LB soft-limits applied to prevent retry amplification.

Outcome: by 09:35 PST we observed 5xx rate drop from ~14% to 1.2% and 429s returned to baseline within 18 minutes. Tail latency returned to expected ranges.

Immediate next steps:
1) Postmortem ticket SUP-9812 opened (link below). We'll keep it in triage and assign owners for root-cause analysis of quant-profile stability on long-context workloads.
2) We will not re-promote v2.1.4 to production until the runtime team completes a targeted eval against long-sequence request patterns.
3) Marissa to run a regression harness against ClearWave's representative prompt set; schedule results in 48 hours.
4) Commercial: Laura will follow-up on goodwill credit and weekly checkpoints; expect a note by EOD.

Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-9812, https://drive.google.com/file/d/metrics-dashboard

If anything regresses please ring the on-call pager immediately. Apologies for the disruption — we know this is high-impact and we're treating it with priority.

— Markus Klein
Sr. Director, Reliability
Redwood Inference
